topics.topic: Define the image-library event that constitutes successfully opening an image source
questions: What exact image-library event counts as opening the source successfully: recognition and creation of an image object from its header, or successful decoding of its first frame?
What exact image-library event counts as successfully opening the source: return from the open call, successful parsing of the first-frame header and dimensions, or successful loading of that frame?

quotes:
2. The source may be of a format of the imported `SOURCE_FORMATS` constant. A scan decides membership by the
   signature alone (A1 order 6). Decoding is the image library's, restricted to the formats of that constant:
   which of them it detects is the library's decision. A source it cannot open as one of them is
   `unreadable_image`, whatever dimensions its header declares; for a source it opens the checks below apply. Checks run in this order: a first frame above the pixel
   limit (width times height) fails with `too_many_pixels`, a source that cannot be decoded with
   `unreadable_image`, and a result above the Portal's read limit with `too_large`. A value equal
   to a limit passes. Only the first frame of an animated image is delivered.
| 4 | A2 rule 2 fails | `TOO_MANY_PIXELS`, `UNREADABLE_IMAGE` or `TOO_LARGE`, as that rule decides |
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats successful header recognition and construction of the library's lazy image object as opening, so it checks the declared pixel count first and returns TOO_MANY_PIXELS; another requires successful loading of the first frame, so corrupt pixel data returns UNREADABLE_IMAGE regardless of the declared dimensions. The calling flow and owner observe the different placement failure member.
judgement.why: The rules order the pixel-count and decoding failures but do not define whether the library has opened a source before or only after its first frame is successfully loaded.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has no placement for an allowed-signature source whose header declares more pixels than the limit and whose first-frame pixel data is corrupt, while the image library can construct a lazy image object from its header.
events: Syncthing places the source in the project's photo folder.
The calling flow scans the project and receives the source as ready because its signature passes A1 order 6.
The calling flow requests delivery of the source.
The deliverer invokes the image library and evaluates A2 rule 2.
outcomes: The returned lazy image object counts as a successful opening, so the earlier pixel-count check fails with the TOO_MANY_PIXELS member.
Opening is not successful until the first frame loads, so the corrupt frame fails with the UNREADABLE_IMAGE member regardless of its declared dimensions.
witness.observer: The calling flow and owner see different placement failure members.
basis:
The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its
publication. When to scan, what to deliver next, what to repeat and which failure to treat as temporary
belong to the calling flow.

3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. A named file that passes condition 1 of rule 5 and that A1 orders 1 and 2 do not reject from its
   metadata is opened, and unless the opening decides A1 order 3 or 5, read once; the bytes that were read
   are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.

A source it cannot open as one of them is
   `unreadable_image`, whatever dimensions its header declares; for a source it opens the checks below apply. Checks run in this order: a first frame above the pixel
   limit (width times height) fails with `too_many_pixels`, a source that cannot be decoded with
   `unreadable_image`, and a result above the Portal's read limit with `too_large`.

questions: Name the UNREADABLE_IMAGE member of = models.PlacementFailure by its member name beside the enumeration address.
